title: Cutover anchor timeline and smoke-test catalog — APR 2026 (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, action-oriented cheat sheet for next-quarter cutovers. Focus: 1) anchor timeline (what MUST happen and when), 2) concise smoke / acceptance checks for each service tier, 3) clear rollback triggers and quick mitigations.

Audience:
- Release engineers coordinating cutover
- On-call SREs for the release window
- PMs/SDEs owning features in the ship

Notes to self (context):
- This is intentionally terse — long playbooks live elsewhere. Use this as the single-pane checklist during the 2-hour cutover window.
- Designed for cross-region releases where we have canary + regional ramp.
- Prioritize low-latency critical paths (API generation, auth, KV cache) over background batch jobs.

High-level rollout model (assumptions):
- Canary (10 hosts) -> regional ramp (50% traffic) -> global flip.
- Autoscale groups are enabled; burst capacity in region B for 15 minutes on failover.
- Fallback model chain: latest-quantized -> stable-quantized -> float-32 stable.

Anchor timeline (T relative to scheduled cutover start):
- T-72h: Freeze branch for shipping artifacts. Finalize feature flags to flip at T+30m and T+60m. Owner: release lead.
- T-24h: Verify infra runbooks and paging roster published. Confirm SLO/alert thresholds. Owner: SRE lead.
- T-2h: Preflight smoke on staging replication: telemetry ingestion, model invocation latency, KV cache priming. Any failure -> delay by 1h and triage. Owner: release engineer.
- T-30m: Canary deploy (10 hosts) in us-west; traffic router rule set to 5% traffic. Run canary validations (see smoke checklist).
- T+15m: Canary health check window complete. If canary passes, scale canary to 25% and start region ramp.
- T+45m: Regional ramp at 50% traffic. Begin sampling 1% of production tokens for quality metrics.
- T+1h30m: Global flip candidate. Confirm no P0/P1 alerts and token cost delta within expected budget band.
- T+2h: Full flip. Post-cutover soak for 4h with increased telemetry retention for token-level traces.

Quick abort/rollback decision tree (short):
- Immediate rollback triggers (abort to previous deployment):
  - P0: model-serving latency > 3x baseline for >5m AND error rate > 2%
  - P0: KV cache miss storm causing 5xx cascade (>1% of requests)
  - P0: authentication failures affecting >0.5% of requests for 10m
  - P1: sustained quality regression measured by eval suite (precision drop > 8% over baseline on sampled prompts)
- Rollback steps (fast):
  1) Disable router rule for new variant (immediate traffic shift to previous) — Routing lead.
  2) Trigger autoscaler to drain new hosts; set scale-in cooldown to 0 — Infra lead.
  3) Re-enable known-good model variant pinning; clear canary tags — Release engineer.
  4) Notify #release-ops with incident summary and status update — Incident lead.
  5) Start postmortem stub (link to RELEASE-xxxx) — PM.

Smoke / acceptance catalog (short checks you run at each step):
- Canaries (must pass all):
  - /health: 200, uptime >= 300s, KV cache warm keys > 95%
  - sample-generation (10 quick prompts): tokens/sec within 20% of baseline, no decoding OOMs
  - auth: token validation success 100% for synthetic test account
  - telemetry: traces show KV latency < 20ms median, 95th < 100ms
  - error budget check: no spike in 5xx (>0.5% above baseline)

- Regional ramp (must pass 80% of checks):
  - endpoint tail latency (p95) within 1.5x baseline for 30m window
  - cost-per-token delta within forecast +/- 8%
  - prefix cache hit rate stable or improving
  - integration checks: embeddings endpoint returns vectors stable norm for sample inputs

- Post-flip soak (must pass monitoring for 4h):
  - consumer-facing auth flows validated across 3 major regions
  - pipeline backfills complete (no backlog > 30m)
  - A/B quality monitors show no negative drift beyond threshold

Telemetry and sampling plan (short):
- Token sampling: 1% of tokens during ramp, 5% during soak for first 30m post-flip.
- Eval probes: run nightly evals against sample prompt-set (small 200 prompt set) to detect subtle regressions.
- Tracer tags: include release-tag header on all canary/ramp calls for easy filtering.

Operational reminders (small but important):
- Pager ownership: explicit handoff 30m prior to T-0. Name in the window: SRE on-call + release engineer primary.
- Communication cadence: status every 15m in #release-ops; immediate update on aborts or escalations.
- Permissions: ensure release lead has router and autoscaler privileges (documented in infra playbook).
- Data compliance: if PII-invoking routes are changed, inform security lead prior to T-0.

Checklist (tick when done) — preflight items:
- [ ] Build artifacts uploaded and checksums validated
- [ ] Feature flags preconfigured and tested (toggle ids documented)
- [ ] Runbook copies linked in Slack and Confluence (quick links posted to #release-ops)
- [ ] Smoke test scripts available and run locally by release engineer
- [ ] Backup traffic routing plan validated (DNS TTLs, fallback BGP prep)
- [ ] Telemetry retention increase scheduled for post-flip 4h period

Open questions / TODOs:
- Who owns the quantized fallback warm-up? (Evan assigned but need confirmation)
- Confirm token sampling threshold is acceptable to privacy/compliance (Maya to confirm)
- Add a quick synthetic load generator for prefix cache warm-up (ticket created: RELEASE-1431)
- Decide whether to run the nightly eval probe earlier for zero-day quality checks — ops suggestion: run small probe T-6h.

Draft release notes snippet (for product/marketing to adapt):
- Release summary: incremental improvements to inference runtime focused on latency and cache efficiency. Includes new router fallback chain designed to reduce outage blast radius.
- User-visible changes: improved cold-start latency on generation endpoints (typical improvement 15–30%), more consistent embedding norms for short inputs.
- Operational notes: deploy uses canary-first model with automated rollback triggers. Increased telemetry retention for initial soak.
- Known issues: small subset of legacy integrations may require toggling model-version pinning (documented in support KB).

Post-cutover follow-ups (owners):
- 24h: reconcile token cost delta and post-release budget impact — Finance liaison
- 48h: full postmortem draft (if any material incidents) — Release lead
- 7d: quality regression check using expanded eval set (Research/Applied ML)

Slack shortlinks to use during the window:
- #release-ops (primary)
- #sre-oncall
- #product-ships

End quick sheet. Keep this copy as the canonical short checklist for the window — long-form runbook: Confluence/Cutover Playbook.

Revision history:
- 2026-04-02: initial draft by Priya Nandakumar
- 2026-04-05: added rollback decision tree (Jordan Lee)
- 2026-04-10: refined smoke checks and telemetry plan (Maya Patel)
